entities.summary: Hrant Dink was a Turkish-Armenian intellectual, editor-in-chief of Agos, journalist, and columnist. As editor-in-chief of the bilingual Turkish-Armenian newspaper Agos, Dink was a prominent member of the Armenian minority in Turkey best known for advocating Turkish–Armenian reconciliation and human and minority rights in Turkey. He was often critical of both Turkey's denial of the Armenian genocide and of the Armenian diaspora's campaign for its international recognition. Dink was prosecuted three times for "insulting Turkishness", while receiving numerous death threats from Turkish nationalists.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hrant Dink's advocacy for Turkish-Armenian reconciliation and human rights in Turkey had significant regional impact, particularly in normalizing relations between Armenia and Turkey. His work also influenced the international recognition of the Armenian genocide.
